page: Microsoft Azure FX4ms_v2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores, operating at a base clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1D cache. It is equipped with 84.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 21.0 GB per core. The instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks reveal strong single-core capabilities, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2353.0, placing it in the top tier. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance at 34.8 GB/sec and 14.49 GB/sec respectively. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks show some tradeoffs. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is weak at 4441.77, and uncached large-block memory read/write speeds are relatively low at 36.48 GB/sec and 25.67 GB/sec. LLM inference speeds are average for small models but drop significantly for larger models, reflecting the 4-vCPU limit.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX4ms_v2 offers a high density of memory relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable choice for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing, and lightweight web serving. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage, which should be factored into the architectural design.
